title: Capacity cushion trigger worksheet + pricing sanity check
body:
Purpose:
A compact working worksheet to map a near-term headcount buffer (capacity cushion), define concrete pricing-sensitivity breakpoints, and codify the operational triggers we would execute if token price/margin moves breach thresholds. This is intentionally lightweight — a surface level sanity check to inform an ops playbook and the upcoming exec review.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Current runway: ~14 months at plan baseline (as of 2026-07 close).
- Nominal hiring plan: +24 headcount over next 6 months (mix: 9 Eng, 4 SRE, 3 Product, 4 CS/Onboarding, 4 Ops/Support).
- Cushion proposal: hold a 6-headcount hiring reserve (floating hires) that releases only if net revenue across the next 90 days tracks to plan.
- Pricing sensitivity: a sustained -12% effective price per token vs. plan triggers hiring pause; -22% triggers broader cost reduction (non-critical hiring freeze + temporary slab-rate cuts for contractors).

Key assumptions (simplified):
- Baseline revenue mix: Hosted API 62%, Dedicated 25%, Private 13%.
- Avg realized price per 1M tokens (plan): $1,500 (hosted mix avg after discounts).
- Avg contribution margin per 1M tokens (plan): 58% (post-GPU, infra, and direct cloud costs).
- Monthly cash burn (org-level): $3.1M baseline plan.
- FTE fully-loaded monthly cost (average): Eng $17.5k, SRE $18.5k, Product $15k, CS/Onboard $11k, Ops/Support $10k.
- Contractor pool monthly cost: $180k baseline.
- GPU-inference marginal cost sensitivity: each 10% drop in price realized while demand constant reduces margin by ~8 p.p. (rough approximation from cost-model v0.9).

Headcount phasing (target hires and cushion):
| Role         | Hires planned (next 6mo) | Cushion reserve | Release condition |
|--------------|--------------------------:|----------------:|------------------|
| Eng (FE/BE)| 9                       | 3               | 90d revenue >= plan + <10% variance |
| SRE         | 4                       | 1               | Observability SLAs stable 60d |
| Product     | 3                       | 0               | Product milestones met (alpha -> beta) |
| CS/Onboard  | 4                       | 1               | Customer NPS / churn signals normal |
| Ops/Support | 4                       | 1               | Ops event rate < baseline threshold |
Total planned hires: 24, total cushion: 6 (carry-forward to H2 if unreleased).

Pricing sensitivity scenarios (hosted-focused lens):
Scenario A — Mild downside (-12% price):
- Effective price per 1M tokens = $1,320.
- Contribution margin drops from 58% -> ~49.5%.
- Monthly burn impact: +$210k (lower contribution).
- Recommended actions: hold cushion hires (freeze 6), pause non-essential contractor spend ($60k target reduction), delay marketing campaign Q4.
- Runway impact: runway shortens by ~1.2 months if actions not taken.

Scenario B — Moderate downside (-22% price):
- Effective price per 1M tokens = $1,170.
- Contribution margin ~40%.
- Monthly burn impact: +$520k.
- Recommended actions: immediate hiring freeze across non-customer-facing roles, reduce contractor pool by 50% ($90k reduction), negotiate short-term GPU vendor credits, implement tiered feature gating for low-margin traffic.
- Operational trigger: if 30-day rolling revenue delta <= -20% vs plan.

Scenario C — Upside (+10% price):
- Effective price per 1M tokens = $1,650.
- Contribution margin ~64.5%.
- Monthly burn improvement: -$280k (extra cushion).
- Recommended actions: consider accelerating 60% of cushion hires, prepay seasonal GPU credits to lock margin, top up reserve runway.

Break-even thresholds (simplified):
- Holding cushion (6 hires) saves ~ $660k/month in fully-loaded run-rate once hires delayed (6 * avg FTE 11k monthly across mixed roles).
- To offset a sustained -22% price move, we need ~ $500–650k/month in cost reductions (hiring pause + contractors + discrete vendor negotiations).

Trigger matrix (concrete, actionable):
- Metric: 30d rolling revenue vs plan. Action timeline: 0–30d, 31–60d, 61–90d.
- Delta band >= -10%: move to hold cushion; delay non-critical hires. Finance to confirm runway daily. (Owner: Finance Ops)
- Delta band -11% to -20%: implement hiring freeze, reduce contractor pool, re-prioritize feature releases (Product + Eng to triage low-margin work). (Owner: CFO + VP Eng)
- Delta band <= -21%: escalate to Exec; open temporary expense reduction plan including discretionary travel, external events, and vendor contract re-bids. (Owner: CEO/CFO)

Operational playbook (short checklist):
- Immediate (within 72h of hitting trigger): pause hiring approvals for roles flagged as cushion; inform recruiting to pause external outreach for non-critical reqs.
- 10-day window: run a 10-line review with Product, Eng, SRE to estimate scope cuts that reduce gross token consumption by low-value paths (embed caching, knob down streaming defaults).
- 30-day window: implement contractor reductions and vendor credit negotiations.
- 60-day window: reforecast full P&L and present to Exec with 3 scenarios.

Financial calculations (worked example for Scenario B):
- Baseline monthly contribution = revenue_monthly * 0.58. Assume revenue_monthly = $5.5M -> baseline contribution = $3.19M.
- Scenario B contribution = 5.5M * 0.40 = $2.2M -> delta = -$990k contribution.
- Countermeasures available (sum): hiring pause = $360k/mo, contractor cuts = $90k/mo, vendor negotiations + GPU credits target = $180k/mo => total ~ $630k. Net shortfall remaining = $360k -> require additional measures (defer product projects / small headcount reductions) to fully cover.

Open questions / unknowns to resolve in next 7 days:
- Does existing committed customer mix have contractual minimums that change effective realized price exposure? (CS to confirm top-10 customers)
- Are there prepay/commit options with our GPU vendors that would materially change the marginal cost curve for a 6–12 month horizon? (Infra to quantify)
- How elastic is demand if we throttle low-margin traffic? Are we cannibalizing high-margin revenue? (Product + Analytics to simulate).

Next steps / owners:
- Finance Ops (Marco Nguyen): finalize a locked-down 90-day trigger sheet and attach to FIN-4321. Due: 2026-08-14.
- Product (Priya Menon): scoped list of low-margin features to gate and estimated reduction in token consumption. Due: 2026-08-10.
- Infra (Samir Kaur): vendor negotiation plan + prepay sensitivity analysis (GPU credits). Due: 2026-08-18.
- CS (Elena Torres): customer contract quick-review for price floors and minimums. Due: 2026-08-12.

Notes on modeling limitations (callouts):
- This is a high-level, conservative sanity model. We intentionally use round numbers and one-line mappings from price to margin; the engineering cost model (cost-model v0.9) includes richer time-of-day and batch efficiency effects that could materially alter the margin impact.
- We should run a second-pass Monte Carlo with token-mix granularity (hosted vs dedicated vs private) before finalizing any layoffs or long-term hiring decisions.

Appendix (quick reference figures):
- Baseline runway months: 14 
- Baseline monthly burn: $3.1M
- Cushion hires held: 6 (saves ~ $660k/mo if fully withheld)
- Contractor pool baseline: $180k/mo
- Pricing sensitivity breakpoints: -12% -> hold cushion; -22% -> hiring freeze + mid-cost measures; <= -30% -> Exec escalation + revenue preservation mode.

End of worksheet.

(Working draft — comments welcome in the doc. This sheet intentionally short, actionable, and designed to be composed into a one-page slide for Friday's exec review.)
